A.trend: Index series is labelled estimate and has no source. The anchor allows 1.
A.comparison: The ratio table uses estimated index values only.
A.chart: The memory chart is honestly labelled estimate.
A.drilldown: Layers are named generically and only 1 of 6 follow-ups executed.
A.export: The estimate CSV is labelled, but it is unmeasured.
A.repro: None of the 14 numbers trace, and the ceiling is 0.
A.accuracy: Its estimated ordering (export controls ≥ TSMC) contradicts the reference: TSMC has 36,563 articles and export controls 7,399. The estimate label softens this but does not remove it.
A.limits: It is specific about what is unmeasured: match mode, window gap, overlap.
A.verdict: An honest non-answer resting on a wrong estimated ordering.
A.facets: Facets are answered from memory only.

B.trend: Full traced 24-month series with window and censoring. Endpoint changes recompute exactly (+125.6%, +169.5%, +286.3%). The Oct-2025 spike is mentioned but its value is not stated in the prose, and there is no decomposition.
B.comparison: Ratios 0.29× and 0.058× and deltas 91,488 and 120,652 recompute exactly, with the overlap caveat. It does not address the spike-vs-baseline contrast the question poses.
B.chart: The single volume chart is fully traced, but tone and critical share are not charted although the data supports them.
B.drilldown: One monthly layer. Only 1 of 4 follow-ups worked.
B.export: Two traced CSVs with provenance and a JSON block, referenced from the prose.
B.repro: 29 of 31 numbers trace. The c1 entry lacks feature and args in the prism-calls block, though they appear in the provenance JSON.
B.accuracy: Figures match the reference and fields are read cautiously. The index partition-check claim is not visible in the record.
B.limits: Window, the 144-day gap and censoring are stated correctly, but mostly in the limits section rather than at the numbers.
B.verdict: Has answer, decision and confidence. It does not name the strongest contrary point: export-control growth is driven by one spike.
B.facets: Volume, share, trend and tone ratios are covered, and overlap is flagged.

C.trend: Endpoint ratios are exact. Peaks are named with values and dates (Feb-25 9,428; Apr-26 9,935; Oct-25 1,773 against 195 and 341). Critical_pct ranges are traced. The chart samples points rather than plotting the full series.
C.comparison: Its own baseline is defined (TSMC mean 1,523/mo) and the ratios recompute (3.5×, 0.20×, 17×, 1.53×). It carries the overlap and sum caveat.
C.chart: Points trace, but semiconductor is omitted, only subsampled months are plotted, tone is not charted, and the 'supports' field cites a critical_pct claim the chart does not show.
C.drilldown: Term, month and tone layers. 6 of 6 follow-ups are on-topic and executable, but none were run and folded back, and there are no item identifiers.
C.export: The monthly CSV holds only selected months (marked partial). The totals CSV is complete. This is at the ceiling.
C.repro: 76 of 81 numbers trace. Derived numbers are recomputable, and calls are listed with args.
C.accuracy: All values match. It catches anomalies: tool growth vs endpoint ratio, undefined critical/tone_ratio/vs_baseline, generic-term over-count, and the combined total being an undeduplicated sum.
C.limits: Limits are specific: censoring, 4.7-month gap, match mode, overlap, export-controls not chip-specific. It states what cannot be answered.
C.verdict: Answer, decision, confidence with reason and a change condition. It names the unexplained spike and is concise.
C.facets: Volume, share, trend, tone/critical, spike and overlap are all grounded.

D.accuracy: No contradictions because nothing is asserted.
D.limits: Honest and specific about what is unmeasurable.
D.verdict: A correct refusal, but it gives no answer.

A: Estimated ordering (chip export controls ≥ TSMC, ratio ~3:1:1) contradicts the reference: TSMC 36,563 vs export controls 7,399
B: Claims the coverage passed index partition-read/row-floor checks; this is not visible in the reference record
C: Coverage figure '107.1% of expected row floor' is not visible in the reference record
Monthly CSV and chart subsample months instead of exporting the full 24-point series

raw.verdict: B and C both reported traced figures from the same news.compare call. C went further: it decomposed critical share by term, named the peaks and the October 2025 export-control spike (1,773 vs 195 the month before), and flagged undefined fields and the generic-term over-count. B instead gave cleaner, complete exports. A gave an estimated term ordering that contradicts the measured data, and D gave no answer at all.
